On this page

TM5-style spectral mass fluxes ​

This page specifies TM5SpectralFluxes, a second construction of the ERA5 spectral mass fluxes for lat-lon (LL), reduced-Gaussian (RG) and direct cubed-sphere (CS) targets. It follows the TM5 meteorological preprocessor (tmm): the face fluxes are quadratures of the retained spectral winds and surface pressure along the target faces, an independent vertical flux is integrated from the spectral divergence, and the horizontal fluxes are balanced layer by layer against the hybrid mass tendency. The existing construction (face- and centre-sampled winds times a face pressure thickness, see ERA5 spectral path) stays the default; the design calls it PointSampledSpectralFluxes.

LL and RG are implemented by TM5-FLUX-1; direct CS is implemented by TM5-FLUX-2b. The point-sampled construction stays the default. Select the new route explicitly:

toml
[preprocessing]
spectral_flux_construction = "tm5_spectral"
spectral_synthesis = "cpu" # reference; omit for GPU (CLI loads CUDA)
# spectral_synthesis_float = "auto" # GPU: auto, Float64 or Float32
# face_quadrature = "gauss_fourier" # LL/RG default
# To select TM5 trapezoids instead:
# face_quadrature = "tm5_trapezoid"
# quadrature_refinement_steps = 2

[numerics]
flux_time_sampling = "window_mean"

The selector is spectral_flux_construction, since the existing flux_construction settings describe the face-method family. Existing configs keep their interpretation and default arithmetic. The new route requires a global target, the hourly ERA5 interval and dry basis, a next-day 00 UTC spectral and humidity endpoint, and retained native interfaces (echlevs or layer merging). Pressure-overlap vertical remapping is outside this construction. The hybrid-B extent must run from 0 to 1, with level_top=1 and zero top A. These contracts are checked during configuration planning, before reading meteorology. GPU selection on the legacy point-sampled route is rejected explicitly; its opt-in is deferred.

The page follows the design of 2026-10-30 with the owner answers of that day. Statements marked estimate are estimates, not measurements.

Sources ​

TM5 citations are file:line in the NOAA CarbonTracker TM5 repository (ct-unified-github at commit 2d60209); pydyn citations are at pydyn commit 0db6e6d. pydyn is a NumPy transcription of the TM5 dynamic core; it starts from the TM5 meteorological archive and has no spectral stage.

Conventions ​

  • Longitude λ, latitude φ, μ=sin⁡φ, g=9.80665 m s⁻². R is the radius of the target mesh (EARTH_RADIUS = 6.371e6 m, equal to TM5's ae, binas:51); it sets face lengths and cell areas. Rv is the vod2uv radius that enters U and V (§2). TM5 uses R=Rv = ae; after owner decision Q4 the two differ.

  • Layers count from the top (k=1) to the surface (k=N); interface e is the top of layer e, so interfaces run e=1…N+1. Hybrid interfaces are pe=Ae+Beps, with ΔAk=Ak+1−Ak and ΔBk=Bk+1−Bk≥0. TM5's FillMassChange takes abs(db) (g3d:366), so the sign convention of ΔB does not matter there.

  • H=ln⁡ps (the spectral LNSP field). Fluxes Fu, Fv and the vertical flux W are rates in kg s⁻¹ integrated over the whole face. Raw W is upward-positive; our stored cm is downward-positive.

  • TM5 and pydyn arrays are bottom-up. Every reference comparison goes through one explicit level-order and sign adapter.

1. Truncation, refinement and ring evaluation ​

Retained truncation. TM5 keeps the source truncation: ShTruncation = T (gi:1587). For ERA5 this is TL639. The existing route synthesises at the target truncation (target_spectral_truncation, T=Nλ/2−1 on LL).

LL/RG face integration. face_quadrature = "gauss_fourier" is the TM5SpectralFluxes default. Gauss–Legendre nodes integrate UΔp/cos⁡φ along meridians. Longitude products are synthesized on an oversampled ring, Fourier transformed, multiplied by the exact interval factor Δλsinc(mΔλ/(2π))eimΔλ/2, and evaluated at target interval starts. Frequency folding before the inverse FFT handles arbitrary RG boundary counts without an LCM-sized synthesis grid. Cell pressure and independent divergence forcing use the same Gauss/Fourier box integrals.

For a latitude width Δφ in radians, the measured rule uses Nφ=max(10,⌈(T+2)Δφ⌉+3) nodes: 10 at T255 and 15 at T639 on 1° faces. Longitude ring length is the smallest multiple of the cell's longitude count exceeding 10(T+2). This oversampling resolves the nonlinear ps=exp⁡H product; exact Fourier integration by itself does not remove aliasing. §13 reports the resolution measurements and doubled reference checks. Polar Gauss nodes are open; their Legendre tables use cos⁡φ directly to avoid cancellation in 1−sin2⁡φ.

Explicit TM5 trapezoids. face_quadrature = "tm5_trapezoid" selects the previous LL/RG integration, with quadrature_refinement_steps = 2 by default:

r(T,Δ)=max(1,⌈nstepΔsT⌉),sT=360°2(T+1).

TM5 uses 2 despite comments saying "5 points per sh resolution" (gi:1602–1630,1677,1822,2458). A 1° edge has 3 subdivisions at T255 and 8 at T639. The refinement-16 proposal was rejected on cost. The explicit rule retains our existing open polar policy and complete wind transform; it does not restore TM5's other numerical errors. CS keeps its established cardinal-16 arc integration and refinement 2 (§10); this selector changes LL/RG coordinate faces.

Oversampled rings. For K output longitudes, TM5 doubles L until J=KL≥2T+1, runs one FFT of length J and keeps every L-th value (gts:1687–1692, gts:1731). The existing fill_ring_spectrum! (src/Preprocessing/Spectral/spectral_synthesis.jl) already supports this: on a buffer of length J≥2T+1, ring_max_wavenumber(T, J) = T, so every retained zonal wavenumber is synthesised. The unnormalised bfft is kept.

Legendre corner. TM5 sets PTT=0 deliberately (gts:713, gts:829–830). compute_legendre_column! evaluates it; this is a documented difference (§13).

CPU cost and golden cases. See §13 for complete changing-hour window measurements, memory and the golden decision. The former refinement-16 proposal cost 6.08× at T255 and 17.10× at T639 (2,577 s/window) and was replaced by Gauss/Fourier integration.

2. Vorticity and divergence to pseudo-winds ​

With

δmn=−1nn2−m24n2−1,σmn=−mn(n+1)

(gts:2037, gts:2042), the spectral coefficients of U=ucos⁡φ and V=vcos⁡φ are

Unm=Rv[δmnζn−1m+iσmnDnm−δm,n+1ζn+1m],Vnm=Rv[−δmnDn−1m+iσmnζnm+δm,n+1Dn+1m]

(gts:1837–1849). TM5's shi_vod2uv treats the truncation edge as follows:

RowTM5 (gts:1949–2045)
m=n=0upper-neighbour term only (gts:1993–1994)
n=T−1, m≤T−2upper neighbour ζT, DT omitted (gts:2013–2014)
n=m=T−1the (m,m) branch: iσ term and upper neighbour (T−1,T) included (gts:1996–1997)
n=T, m≤T−1lower neighbour only: the iσ term and the upper neighbour are dropped (gts:2021–2022)
(T,T)zero (gts:2030–2031)

The source gives EMOS compatibility as the reason (vorticity and divergence assumed truncated at T−1, gts:1851–1852). For Rv it uses ae, 6.371 × 10⁶ m (gts:1951).

Ours is the existing vod2uv! (src/Preprocessing/Spectral/spectral_synthesis.jl): it keeps every neighbour term inside [m,T], truncates the output at n=T and uses IFS_EARTH_RADIUS, 6.371229 × 10⁶ m, for Rv: the radius consistent with the ERA5 coefficients (owner decision Q4). The relative radius difference is 3.6×10−5.

Remaining truncation. For vorticity and divergence truncated at T, the wind has a nonzero degree T+1: UT+1m=Rvδm,T+1ζTm and VT+1m=−Rvδm,T+1DTm. TM5 and the legacy vod2uv! drop this row. The new construction's complete_wind_coefficients retains it, using the existing transform within [m,T] and adding the exact neighbour at T+1. This is required for the Gauss test to converge for a source mode at degree T. The single-mode tests size both retained contributions explicitly.

3. Cell surface pressure: the discrete rule ​

TM5 evaluates eH at the refined sample points (gi:1893), integrates each refined row with piecewise-linear interval quadrature in λ (IntervalQuad_Lin, gi:1907), integrates the row results with cosine-weighted linear quadrature in φ (IntervalQuad_Cos_Lin, gi:1926) and divides by the cell area (key 'exp,aver', tmm:1876). The cell value p¯s,c is therefore the exact integral of a piecewise-linear interpolant of eH; it is neither ∬eHdA/Sc nor exp of the mean of H. Explicit tm5_trapezoid retains this rule. The default gauss_fourier instead integrates the sampled exponential with Fourier longitude intervals and Gauss latitude weights times cos⁡φ, approximating the actual area mean ∬eHdA/Sc (§1/§13). Neither rule is the exponential of mean H. The layer mass remains

Mc,k=Scg(ΔAk+ΔBkp¯s,c).

4. Horizontal face fluxes per native layer ​

For a meridional face at λf between φS and φN, and a zonal face at φf between λW and λE,

Ff,ku=Rg∫φSφNUk(λf,φ)cos⁡φ[ΔAk+ΔBkeH(λf,φ)]dφ,Ff,kv=Rg∫λWλEVk(λ,φf)[ΔAk+ΔBkeH(λ,φf)]dλ

(tmm:2135–2138, tmm:2167–2170; integrands gi:3429 and gi:3784; units kg s⁻¹, tmm:1966). Native-layer fluxes are summed into the retained layers (FillLevels(..., 'sum'), tmm:2147, tmm:2179). The product of a mean wind and a mean face thickness is not this integral: the covariance of wind and surface pressure along the face matters. TM5 also integrates face surface pressures (spu, spv, tmm:2142, tmm:2174); the plan does not need them.

Poles. TM5's IntLon gives zero meridional flux at either pole (gi:3781–3782); ours does the same. TM5 has two polar-row quirks:

  • IntLat sets the pole sample to the sum of the adjacent row divided by size(llf, 1). That row holds the Nλ+1 face longitudes 0…Nλ, so TM5 divides by Nλ+1 and counts the periodic face twice (gi:3373, gi:3396, gi:3444).

  • IntArea_shi_ll_fgh uses the adjacent-row mean at the pole even for the Dcos⁡φ integrand, which is zero there (gi:2498–2511, gi:2588–2593).

The construction uses open (pole-free) quadrature nodes in the polar rows instead; the difference is listed in §13.

5. Independent vertical flux ​

Per native layer, TM5 integrates the horizontal mass divergence directly from the spectral fields. With the two radii of the conventions, the implemented form is

Ck=RRvg∬Dk(ΔAk+ΔBkeH)cos⁡φdλdφ+Rg∬eHΔBkcos⁡φ(Uk∇λH+Vk∇φH)dλdφ,

with ∇λH=∂H/∂λ and ∇φH=(1−μ2)∂H/∂μ (tmm:2428, tmm:2446, tmm:2450, combined at tmm:2468). TM5 writes the first factor as R2/g (tmm:2468) because it has R=Rv. Applying Gauss's theorem to the face fluxes of §4 gives exactly this expression: the divergence D is defined on the IFS sphere of radius Rv, U and V carry Rv, and the face lengths carry R. The design note wrote R2/g; that is corrected here. With R2/g, W and the convergence of the face fluxes would differ by 3.6×10−5 of the D term in every layer, and the discrete Gauss test of §14 would stall at that level. Ck is the layer-integrated divergence g−1∬∇⋅(vΔpk)dA [kg s⁻¹]. With the downward partial sums Ie=∑k<eCk and the column total Is=∑kCk,

We=Ie−BeIs,W1=WN+1=0

is the upward vertical mass flux at interface e (tmm:2466–2473, tmm:2517, tmm:2522; TM5 forms BeIs−Ie and negates it at tmm:2568). It satisfies the hybrid layer budget −Ck+Wk+1−Wk=−ΔBkIs. Retained interfaces are selected, not summed: FillLevels (call at tmm:2558) chooses the fill mode 'combine' when the target levels are a selection of the source levels (hyb:1050–1058, hyb:2408–2420). The key 'bottom' passed at tmm:2558 is used only by the 'interpol' mode (hyb:2436–2438).

W must come from the spectral divergence, not from the finite-volume divergence of the target fluxes; otherwise the per-layer constraint of §6 becomes circular.

Spectral gradient. For X=H, the meridional gradient coefficients are

(∇φH)nm=(n+2)εm,n+1Hn+1m−(n−1)εm,nHn−1m,εm,n=n2−m24n2−1,

from (1−μ2)dPnm/dμ=−nεm,n+1Pn+1m+(n+1)εm,nPn−1m. TM5's coefficient comment gives the same rows for n<T (gts:1788–1795). The same comment states the n=T row as −(T−1)εm,TXm,T−1 (gts:1794), but the executable branch computes +(n−1)εm,nXm,n−1 (gts:1804): a sign error. TM5 also truncates the gradient at degree T, dropping the n=T+1 term −Tεm,T+1HTm. The plan computes the exact gradient, with output up to degree T+1 (owner decision Q3). The error reaches W through V∇φH (tmm:2450).

TM5 also computes the surface-pressure tendency tsp (tmm:2499–2507). Only the PRISM coupling path consumes it (met:1645–1718), so the plan does not build it.

6. Per-layer balance ​

TM5 balances each layer's horizontal fluxes against the hybrid mass tendency of the window [a,b]:

M˙k=SgΔBkps(b)−ps(a)b−a

(FillMassChange, g3d:366; met:1798, met:1811). The layer residual is rk=Hk+Wk+1−Wk−M˙k, with Hk the horizontal convergence (GTS:2666–2669, written here top-down). The horizontal target is therefore

Hk∗=M˙k−(Wk+1−Wk),

using the W of the endpoint being balanced. Both endpoint flux sets of a window are balanced against the same M˙k (met:1921–1924, met:2033–2036).

LL solver. Per level, TM5 solves a periodic five-point index-space Poisson problem by FFT: eigenvalues 2(cos⁡(2πi/Nλ)+cos⁡(2πj/Nφ)−2) (GTS:3028), zero mode removed (GTS:3031, GTS:3166), then the west and south gauges are subtracted so the outer faces stay closed (GTS:3172–3192). The per-layer global-mean residual is left uncorrected; it cancels in the column sum. pydyn transcribes this solve (pydyn/balance.py:183–201). Our dry-pin route first makes the target solvable: for cell c, solve against Hc,k∗−(Sc/∑S)∑c′Hc′,k∗. The pressure guard removes only the known global water tendency (§9); final dry repair imposes the dry budget.

CS solver. The direct target uses the same Hk∗ and area-weighted removal of its global mode. The CS face table stores outward-positive flux, so its explicit target is −Hk∗. DirectCSPoisson factors a pinned principal minor of the global degree-four graph Laplacian once per serial run and reuses it for both endpoint sets, every layer and every window. Corrections update canonical and mirror entries with the face table's seam signs. This is TM5's layer equation on our CS graph, rather than TM5's periodic FFT five-point solver. The existing CS PCG endpoint target keeps its historical arithmetic through a neutral target-functor split.

A one-thread CPU synthetic solver benchmark gives the following stage times (68 right-hand sides, graph built independently of meteorology):

GridCellsFactorization68 direct solvesOne PCG solve
C9048,6001.01 s0.46 s0.30 s (705 iterations)
C180194,4000.72 s1.56 s1.59 s (1433 iterations)

The first factorization includes compilation. Process peak RSS was 0.77 GB at C90 and 1.06 GB after C180; these are process peaks, not factor sizes. The smooth synthetic RHS leaves maximum relative direct residuals 5.15×10−9 and 2.49×10−8, respectively, from conditioning of the pinned graph. Acceptance uses the physical pressure-normalized guards below; these timings are neither full-day performance nor GPU measurements.

Guards. CheckMassBalance compares the column convergence with the surface-pressure tendency, relative to the mean surface pressure [s⁻¹] (GTS:2864–2936):

Stagerms limitmax limitOn failure
pre-check10−410−3abort (met:1893–1894, met:1901–1903)
post-check10−710−6repeat the balance, up to MB_MAX_TRIES = 3 passes (met:1445, met:1917–1920), then abort (met:1943–1946, met:2055–2058)

These are repeated Poisson passes, not Richardson extrapolation. pydyn raises on the pre-check (pydyn/balance.py:211) but returns ok = False after the third failed post-check (pydyn/balance.py:212–218), and its forward driver ignores the flag (pydyn/forward.py:134). The construction follows the Fortran and raises an error.

Known difference. The existing balance_mass_fluxes! (src/Preprocessing/Spectral/mass_support.jl) skips a level whose largest absolute residual is below 10−10; TM5 never skips. The skip is harmless and recorded here.

7. Vertical closure and the explicit-dm identity ​

TM5 interpolates the balanced pu, pv to each dynamic-step midpoint (mdat:760, mdat:879; base meteodata.F90:764, :773) and calls dynam0. In bottom-up indexing with P=∑lHl and h=Δt/2 (adv:210), it forms

cml=h[Bl+1P−∑k>lHk]

upward at the upper face of layer l (adv:241–256, adv:265–266, adv:290), with am=hpu and bm=hpv (adv:274, adv:282). The archived vertical flux is not advected. The IO-server B-pivot is disabled in this TM5 version (b_pivot_active = .false., "TODO #332 B-pivot REVERT", acfl:928–938). pydyn transcribes dynam0 as fluxes_from_meteo (pydyn/kernels.py:89–112).

Identity. The existing explicit-dm closure recompute_cm_from_dm_target! (src/MetDrivers/ReplayContinuity.jl) integrates Ck+1=Ck−Dk−Δmk from C1=0 at the top (top-down, downward-positive). In bottom-up form its upward flux at the top of layer l is the mass gained by the layers above it minus what enters them horizontally. With Δmk=h(Bk−Bk+1)P and BL+1=0 at the top,

∑k>l(Δmk−hHk)=h[Bl+1P−∑k>lHk],

which is TM5's cm, with no assumption about the column residual. TM5's sd also sums from the top (adv:253–256); the two differ only in where h and ΔBP are rounded (about 10−12 scaled, not bitwise). The column residual is zero in exact arithmetic; at rounding level, recompute_cm_from_dm_target! folds it back over the column. With the endpoint Δm the same function is today's explicit-dm closure, so the plan has no separate closure type. recompute_cm_from_divergence! is already the ΔB× pit form and stays a staging helper.

8. Pipeline on LL, RG and CS targets ​

E marks a shared existing function, N a new implemented function.

#StageFunctionsHome

5Dry pin on the integrated PS, fluxes not recomputed (Q1)E pin_global_mean_ps_using_qv!Spectral/mass_support.jl

7Target levelsTM5EndpointPlan prepares plan_vertical once per day; apply_vertical! with MassField and MassFluxField sums; N InterfaceMassFluxField (selects retained interfaces with the body of ConvectionInterfaceFlux); E merge_qv! weighted by the pinned moist masses. The NOAA levels are ml137_tropo34a, not ml137_tropo34.Vertical/, Spectral/
8Per window: balance both endpoint sets against the window's M˙ (§6)balance_window_layers!, balance_tm5_layers!; LL balance_mass_fluxes!, RG balance_compressed_level! with reused DirectRingPoisson; guards and up to three passesTargets/, MassClosure/

11Substep schedule, amounts, column balance, cm, replay gatesE schedule; amounts via MetDrivers.flux_application_seconds; apply_poisson_balance! → balance_column_mass_fluxes! (LL), balance_compressed_column_fluxes! (RG); recompute_cm_from_dm_target! with the dry endpoint ΔmTargets/, MassClosure/, MetDrivers/
12WriteE writers; version-5 header with the construction identityTransportBinary/, MetDrivers/BinaryFormat/

For CS, Spectral/cs_spectral_integrals.jl implements stages 3–4 on regular cell-centred rings without pole nodes. The CS target prepares the shared cs_spectral_face_geometry scalar stencils, face normals and conservative box overlaps once, then supplies them to Spectral without a reverse dependency on MassClosure. CSSpectralIntegralWorkspace applies face and overlap maps on the synthesis backend with portable KernelAbstractions gathers. Refined three-dimensional samples remain there through integration; completed reduced target fields return at the endpoint boundary. CPU surface PS uses Float64; GPU surfaces and three-dimensional kernels follow the selected synthesis precision with typed constants, without Float64 promotion in Float32 kernels.

Targets/CubedSphere/tm5_spectral_day.jl orchestrates the shared post-integral pin and moist merge, per-layer CS balance, adjacent-cell face humidity, endpoint drying and mean. Final dry amounts use the existing CS column balance, diagnose_balanced_cs_cm!, replay and positivity contracts and streaming writer. After residual booking, the direct CS route explicitly zeros the rounded surface-interface remainder before replay, enforcing the closed physical boundary. Positivity retries rebuild amounts from pristine dry rates. The mandatory next-day endpoint closes the final window; no held-endpoint fallback is used. The optional live Calc_Kzz group is assembled through the shared CS PBL writer. Two moist endpoints and one output window are retained.

CS writes TM5SpectralFluxesHeader with unchanged v5 identity fields and no new payload sections. Ordinary provenance keys are cs_face_quadrature = "great_circle_midpoint_cardinal16_v2", samples_per_face, refined_nlon, refined_nlat and cs_cell_quadrature = "conservative_refined_box_mean_v1", plus the actual synthesis backend/precision. Existing v5 LL/RG files require no new keys.

Folders are under src/Preprocessing/ unless they start with MetDrivers/. The order differs on purpose from the existing route:

  • Existing route: pin → recompute fluxes → dry conversion on native levels → merge → column balance → cm.

  • TM5 route: moist integration → pin (no recompute) → moist merge → moist per-layer balance with W → dry conversion of each endpoint set on target layers → window mean → shared dry column balance and closure.

Substep retries. The balanced moist rates [kg s⁻¹] do not depend on the substep schedule, so a positivity-driven retry recomputes only stage 11 from the stored rates; no field already balanced in amount units is rescaled. This is the rule of the cubed-sphere spectral writer (src/Preprocessing/Targets/CubedSphere/cubed_sphere_spectral.jl).

Memory. Both targets decode one spectral hour at a time with ecCodes indexes; the optional decoded cache contains one hour per JLD2 file. The next-day reader also reads only hour 00. Constructed endpoints retain merged PS, mass, humidity, face rates and W, without native C. Only two endpoints survive at a time. RG closes and writes each window immediately. LL closes each window and keeps one completed lookahead window to form the historical delta payload; it retains neither a day of outputs nor a day of pristine rates. Synthesis batches bound the refined-grid field buffers. Surface and 3-D plans share Legendre tables when their precision matches; duplicate face rings share their synthesis. The coefficient working set at T639/L137 is approximately 1.80 GB per hour, plus the required next-day hour (3.60 GB combined), versus 43.25 GB for the previous 24-hour source allocation alone. These decimal sizes exclude plans, quadrature and target buffers. The handoff records the CPU measured extrapolation.

9. Mass consistency under the dry pin ​

TM5 matches the area mean of the total surface pressure to p_global = 98500 Pa by an additive offset (binas:133; met:1535–1537, met:1764–1766; the offset is added uniformly at GTS:1107–1115). We keep our dry pin, pin_global_mean_ps_using_qv!, which shifts the surface pressure additively so that the global dry mass implied by the native humidity equals GLOBAL_MEAN_DRY_SURFACE_PRESSURE (98325 Pa).

  • No normalisation factor is needed. Pin the integrated PS with the same native q that is merged later, then merge q with the pinned moist masses; merge_qv! preserves ∑qM exactly. Together, ∑K(1−q¯K)MK on target layers equals the pinned native dry mass in exact arithmetic.

  • Global water term. The dry pin leaves a global moist tendency equal to the global water change. Before each layer solve, remove the layer's area-weighted global target, so the target is globally solvable. The guard compares the column against the moist tendency minus the known global water tendency distributed by area; global dry-mass drift still fails. This prevents an index-space mean from becoming a polar pressure error. Previously a global fractional water rate G/M appeared as (G/M)(S¯/Sc) in the guard, with mean/min area ratio about 290 at 0.25°. Thus even a 10−9 s⁻¹ global estimate could give nearly 3×10−7 s⁻¹ at the smallest cells. The scaled-cap regression exceeds the old maximum threshold and passes after the source projection. Final dry column repair still imposes the stored dry endpoint budget.

  • Local E − P term. The dry conversion leaves a local column residual of about E−P relative to the column mass (estimate: about 10−9 s⁻¹ for 3 mm per day, up to 3×10−7 s⁻¹ for 10 mm per hour of heavy rain). The shared dry column balance removes it, as in the existing route.

  • q=0 limit. After the column balance, the dry route's cm equals the hybrid-B closure in exact arithmetic (covered by the closure and dry-limit tests).

10. Reduced Gaussian and direct cubed-sphere specifics ​

Owner decision Q11: RG ships with LL from the first flux pull request.

  • Geometry. RG cells are longitude-latitude boxes on each ring with midpoint ring boundaries; meridional faces between rings are latitude-arc segments of the least-common-multiple subdivision (src/Grids/ReducedGaussianMesh.jl).

  • Quadrature. TM5's one-dimensional rules apply exactly with a per-ring Δλ. A prefix integral of the refined samples along each face ring gives every LCM segment in O(1). Each ring's FFT length is a multiple of its Nλ that is at least 2T+1.

  • Balance. Per-level balance on the existing compressed ring Laplacian. The column PCG takes about 19 s per window at O90 (measured, header of src/Preprocessing/MassClosure/ring_poisson_balance.jl); the per-layer route needs 2Nz solves per window, so it needs a factor-once direct solve of the same Laplacian, reused across levels, endpoint sets and windows. The existing column PCG path stays unchanged. On O90 (35,640 cells, 2,250,376 faces), one-thread compression takes 0.18–0.41 s, factorization 0.70–0.88 s, and 68 reused layer solves 0.40–0.43 s.

The direct RG spectral path already shares the LL primitives (ReducedSpectralSynthesis; spectral_to_ring! and compute_reduced_horizontal_fluxes! in src/Preprocessing/Targets/ReducedGaussian/reduced_transport_helpers.jl).

Direct CS quadrature. Let Δmin be the smallest target face length in degrees and r=quadraturerefinement(T,Δmin,nstep). Open, cell-centred synthesis rings have spacing at most Δmin/r and an even longitude count retaining degree T+1. At C90/T639 the shape is 3056×1528; at C90/T255 it is 1528×764. These are oversampled relative to the retained bandwidth. The run cache retains synthesis plans, face/overlap maps and the graph factor across matching days.

For the constant Cartesian normal Nf directed left to right,

Ff,k=1g∫f(vk⋅Nf)(ΔAk+ΔBkeH)dl.

The face map uses tensor-product 16-point cardinal interpolation in longitude and latitude of the sampled Cartesian wind–pressure product. It preserves sampled pressure–wind covariance. It integrates that interpolant with equally spaced midpoints in great-circle arc length, including the slerp Jacobian. This differs from TM5's uniform-latitude/longitude trapezoids of UΔp/cos⁡φ and VΔp. The sample count is N=max(16,4r,⌈(T+2)θmax/0.1⌉), where θmax is the largest target edge angle in radians. It is 112 at C90/T639 and 45 at C90/T255. The tighter midpoint spacing bounds the error of modes oscillating along the face as well as the interpolation error across it. Increasing only the old midpoint count would leave its transverse bilinear damping. The previous 24-point bilinear C90/T639 rule attenuated the 637/637 meridian probe by 20.70%; it is no longer the direct TM5 CS default. The existing point-sampled CS, LL/RG and general LineIntegralFaceFluxes paths retain their original arithmetic.

A zero face integral has no finite relative error. Tests therefore check complex harmonic phases against an absolute integral envelope and also report ordinary relative error when the integral is at least 10% of that envelope. The envelope is the integral of the absolute harmonic amplitude; underflowed modes below 10−13 of the largest envelope are excluded. Every retained scalar harmonic through T255 and T639 is tested on C90-like meridians (including halfway between source longitudes), a tilted actual C90 edge, a polar edge and an equatorial arc, against independent 256-node Gauss integration. Vector harmonics and converged TM5 comparisons are tested in the same file, test_tm5_cs_harmonic_accuracy.jl. The maximum ordinary relative error is 0.04075% against exact integration and 0.04091% against converged TM5; the maximum envelope-normalized error is 0.02747%. These sweeps cover all 205,120 retained scalar modes and both vector families at T639, and all 32,896 at T255, on each of five faces. Selected high modes also exercise the portable gather in Float32 and Float64. This is a measured bound on those faces and test fields, not a theorem for arbitrary pressure spectra: eHv is not band limited even when H and the wind are.

Accuracy reference. The CS path targets converged physical integrals (owner decision, 2026-11-02). Default TM5 IntLon has one-degree retained-mode errors of −18.7414% at T255 and −16.6374% at T639; its default and exact integrals cannot simultaneously satisfy a 0.1% bound. Tests preserve those counterexamples and compare accuracy with the IntLat/IntLon rule at converged refinement (1024 subdivisions). Section 13 gives the measured cause, the comment/code refinement mismatch and the real-ERA5 difference. General tilted CS edges have no corresponding TM5 meridian/parallel face.

Polar evaluation. A scalar transform of pseudo-wind coefficients obtains small U by subtraction before division by cos⁡φ. On the C90/T639 outermost ring at 89.941099°, the Float32 degree-one zonal rotation had 5.9582% relative error (physical u=0.00567218 m/s). CS now evaluates vector harmonics from latitude derivatives of associated Legendre functions where |cos⁡φ|<0.025. Derivative tables use cos⁡φ directly and a differentiated recurrence; their device tables, potential coefficients, GEMMs, FFTs and replacement kernel all use the selected 3-D precision. No Float64 arithmetic is introduced in Float32 device kernels. The same probe's relative error is 4.51×10−7 at T639 and 4.86×10−7 at T255. Tests also exercise tilted rotation and divergent degree-one modes. Selected near-truncation vector modes on production rings have maximum Float32 relative wind error 3.40×10−7 against direct Float64 values. Surface synthesis retains the existing Float64 policy.

The old bilinear source sampler clamps latitude poleward of its outermost ring. The new high-order CS map instead continues Cartesian products through the poles by reflecting latitude and shifting longitude by π. This supplies centred stencils even for face samples closer to a pole than the outermost ring. Neither policy reproduces TM5's duplicate-longitude polar mean or its substituted Dcos⁡φ endpoint. Ordinary LL/RG polar policy is unchanged.

PS remains the conservative overlap mean of eH box samples. Independent Ck retains the same overlap on the §5 forcing density, including Rv/(Rg)DkΔpk and psΔBk(UkHλ+VkHφ)/(Rgcos2⁡φ). Its integral feeds W and the existing layer solve. The face accuracy change does not turn that box rule into an exact spectral cell integral; Gauss/closure/replay tests cover its separate discretization and budget.

Cost and choice. cs_exact_samples supplies a portable, batched direct vector-harmonic evaluation at arbitrary face points without interpolation. It uses selected-precision Legendre/derivative recurrence, Fourier sums and compensated accumulation. Bounded chunks need no per-point Legendre table. A warmed T639 eight-level, 64-point chunk took 1.388 s on one CPU thread. Straight scaling to every C90 face midpoint and two L137 endpoints gives 8.09 million seconds per window, versus 123 seconds for the previous ring-synthesis/face-gather workload. This is an extrapolation of the direct implementation, not an optimized non-uniform FFT or exact-latitude ring implementation. A separate exact-sample-latitude geometry count, grouping absolute latitudes within 10−12 radians and exploiting hemisphere symmetry, finds 685,507 distinct latitudes at C90 and 1,366,010 at C180. A conventional retained Legendre table would require 1.128/2.249 TB in Float64 (half in Float32), or 449/894 times the current latitude-contraction work before exact longitude evaluation. Chunking removes that storage requirement while retaining the contraction work. These are measured geometry counts and storage/work estimates, not NUFFT timings. The measured direct point implementation exceeds the 5× threshold by a wide margin, so the high-order oversampled-ring alternative is the default. Its integrated stencils are combined into one reusable scalar face stencil, with each Cartesian normal stored once. The gather reconstructs weights in the original X/Y/Z order, preserving the expanded map's arithmetic, including zero-normal products. Float32 stores an Int8 rounding offset per component/stencil entry so that the reconstructed weight equals the original once-rounded Float64 geometry product, without Float64 device arithmetic. This avoids both a samples×16² allocation per level and triplicated scalar geometry.

Before geometry compaction, C90/T639 warmed batch costs were 3.376 s for eight-level U/V/D synthesis, 0.143 s for polar replacement and 1.325 s for the face gather (previous gather: 0.201 s). Two L137 endpoint equivalents cost 166 s versus 123 s, a 1.35× ratio. These window estimates exclude common surface/cell overlap, balance, closure and IO work. Setup took 55.6 s for the face map. The former expanded Float64 portable gather stored 1.540 GB, shared synthesis plans 3.129 GB, and polar plans 0.118 GB; estimated live synthesis/face buffers total 7.07 GB, excluding source hourly coefficients, cell overlap and graph factors. Setup temporarily retains the 2.165 GB host sparse map. Sizes are decimal GB; times exclude compilation after warmup except the first geometry setup.

A CPU-only GPU model at 500 GB/s effective gather bandwidth gives 1.41 s per two-endpoint L137 C90 window-equivalent for the new gather alone (1.48 s including the padded final batches). A 1 TFLOP/s FP64 recurrence model gives 27,533 s for the direct point method. These are estimates, not GPU measurements, and omit GEMM/FFT, launch and transfer costs. Actual GPU execution remains untested in this CPU-only run.

The corresponding pre-compaction C180/T639 benchmark retains 3056×1528 rings and uses 56 face midpoints. Warmed eight-level synthesis, polar replacement and gather cost 3.382, 0.133 and 3.853 s; the old gather costs 0.364 s. Two-endpoint L137 equivalents are 252 s versus 128 s (1.97×). The expanded gather stored 4.864 GB, estimated live synthesis/face storage is 10.41 GB, and the temporary host sparse map is 6.595 GB. Face-map setup takes 119.8 s. Direct-point scaling gives 16.20 million CPU seconds per window. Under the same GPU assumptions the new gather is 4.44 s (4.67 s with padding) and the direct recurrence 55,066 s. These timings use Julia and BLAS one thread, batch eight, Float64, with no actual GPU execution. The benchmark is retained at scripts/benchmarks/bench_cs_spectral_quadrature.jl. Set ATMOSTR_BENCH_EXACT_LATITUDES=1 to reproduce the exact-ring geometry count, and ATMOSTR_BENCH_FULL_WINDOW=1 to time complete face-path windows. The latter includes all 36 padded batches plus the production Cartesian pressure–wind/forcing kernel. C90/C180 measured 198.1/292.1 s, with peak process RSS 14.63/23.79 GB, including setup and benchmark scratch in the peak. This still excludes common surface synthesis, cell overlap, balance, closure and IO; it is not a full preprocessing-window timing. The day driver reuses the previous endpoint, so steady-state face work is approximately 99.1 s/window at C90 and 146.1 s/window at C180; a 24-window day builds 25 endpoints, giving approximately 103.2/152.2 s/window before the common stages and amortized setup. The GPU gather model likewise halves to 0.74/2.33 s per steady-state window with endpoint reuse. These full-window timings and GPU models describe the expanded geometry before the storage optimization.

The compact map shares scalar stencil indices/weights and each face normal. A paired CPU benchmark against the pre-compaction fix measures:

Real endpoint check. Local ERA5 T639 GRIB endpoints on 2021-12-01 at 00:00 and 01:00 were checked at native levels 1, 70 and 137 on four C90 faces (central, tilted, polar and panel boundary). Actual ring-synthesized Cartesian pressure–wind products use the production cardinal weights and are compared with 256-node Gauss integration of direct spectral point values. All eight endpoint/face checks pass; maximum scaled relative error is 0.002885%. This checks individual endpoint rates before balancing; it is not a full-day ERA5 W or transport comparison. The reproducible opt-in file is test/real_data/test_tm5_cs_endpoint_accuracy.jl.

T/q merge weights use each construction's stored window-start total surface pressure. Merged T/q can therefore differ between constructions beyond rounding, consistent with each binary's hybrid layers.

12. Binary identity ​

A TM5SpectralFluxes binary is written as format version 5: version 4 plus the construction identity. This part is implemented (TM5-0); see Binary format for the full contract.

Header keyValue
format_version5
flux_construction"tm5_spectral" or "point_sampled_spectral"
flux_construction_revisionrevision of the construction (tm5_spectral only)
spectral_truncation_usedretained truncation T (tm5_spectral only)
face_quadraturegauss_fourier (LL/RG default) or tm5_trapezoid; parsed once into a type
quadrature_refinement_stepsnstep of the explicit trapezoid and CS refinement rule (default 2)
vod2uv_radius_mvod2uv radius in m (tm5_spectral only)

The reader decodes the keys into TM5SpectralFluxesHeader or PointSampledSpectralFluxesHeader; a version-4 header decodes to NoFluxConstructionHeader. Readers accept versions 4 and 5. Writers produce version 5 only when the identity is recorded, so every existing output stays version 4. The mesh radius stays in the existing planet_radius_m. The window flux uses the existing version-4 sampling tags (source_flux_sampling = "window_mean", flux_sampling = "window_constant"); the new LL and RG route records these tags from its construction.

The v5 headers also record spectral_synthesis (cpu/gpu), spectral_synthesis_float (the actual Float64/Float32 plan type), and spectral_surface_float (the actual surface precision). LL/RG Gauss/Fourier products use construction revision 2; explicit trapezoids and the existing CS rule retain revision 1. The face_quadrature tag and Gauss/oversampling resolution fields record the LL/RG quadrature. CUDA's math mode is set to PEDANTIC for each transform and restored even on exceptions; FAST_MATH is rejected.

13. Differences from TM5 ​

We use TM5's spectral budget equations, with the numerical corrections and modelling departures inventoried below; we do not reproduce TM5's numerical errors. In particular, LL/RG now use the Gauss/Fourier reference rule as their default, and the direct CS path targets converged face integrals, rather than agreement with TM5's default under-resolved quadrature (owner decision, 2026-11-02). There is no TM5-default-compatible CS quadrature option. The two groups below distinguish numerical corrections from modelling or convention choices; unisolated sizes are explicitly marked not measured.

For this inventory, paired citations identify the two inspected source trees: R/file:line is relative to tm5-moguntia-r1112-revised/base in the TM5-MP r1112 source tree; C/file:line is relative to base/trunk/src in the CarbonTracker TM5 repository (ct-unified-github). These prefixes do not change the CarbonTracker abbreviations in Sources above. Archive settings and the offline coarsener are configuration choices, not universal properties of either base tree; their additional provenance follows the convention table.

The order was chosen by measurement. Eight nodes passed the retained-harmonic probe but missed the real T255 all-native-level per-face requirement: maximum meridian relative error 4.50e-6 at 01 UTC. Production therefore uses at least 10 nodes, 15 at T639 on 1° faces, and tenfold longitude-product oversampling (§1). Tests sweep every product frequency through 2(T+1) at T255/T639, on 0.5°, 1° and 5° intervals with equatorial and polar origins; every nonzero harmonic integral passes 1e−6 relative error. Analytic null integrals use an absolute tolerance. Independent Fourier-product tests include odd/even FFT lengths and noncommensurate RG interval counts.

Reproduce warmed timing with scripts/benchmarks/bench_tm5_refinement_window.jl CONFIG 2021-12-01 OUT. For isolated RSS, add a fourth argument, tm5_trapezoid or gauss_fourier, in a fresh process per rule. Use a TMPDIR on fast local disk, empty CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and the settings above. Raw timing tables, payload SHA256 checks, the summary FINAL_MEASUREMENTS.json, the accuracy and balanced-flux evidence and the full work record are kept outside the repository. These warmed/isolated results supersede the earlier ordered cold-pair claim.

Golden policy. Only the two O24 configs pin tm5_trapezoid, steps 2. The following golden stage/window figures predate the memory and CPU scheduling revision; they document the retained pin decision rather than current golden throughput. On the frozen T639 input, a warmed eight-level batch cost 3.093/7.939 s (trapezoid/Gauss), 2.57×. With 18 padded native batches and surface work counted once, projected spectral endpoint cost is 2.64×, beyond the ~2× threshold. The two LL72 configs follow Gauss/Fourier: their warmed batch is 2.283/4.414 s (1.93×) and the spectral endpoint projection is 1.96×. These historical projections cover spectral work, not total golden-suite runtime.

Complete changing-hour windows took 150.91/181.60 s (1.20×) on LL72 and 163.92/294.05 s (1.79×) on O24. Their fixed decode/planning/humidity work and first-arm JIT mask the O24 repeated cost; pinning uses the warmed evidence. Live PBL adds shared non-spectral work. The two LL cases pre_ll72_tm5 and pre_ll72_tm5_tm5pbl are stated numerical deltas in masses, pressures and fluxes, with possible pressure-dependent PBL deltas. C24 keeps its existing arc method and restored refinement 2. No golden references are written here. The only defined runtime consumer of these changed cases is run_ll72_tm5_tm5pbl_cpu_f64, which consumes pre_ll72_tm5_tm5pbl; pre_ll72_tm5 has no runtime consumer in cases.toml. Standard golden check resolves @CASE: inputs from the reference tree, so that runtime case's delta needs a separate record/comparison using regenerated inputs. An unchanged runtime check does not test the new preprocessing products. See test/golden/README.md for the case policy.

Transport impact. Over a full T255 day, balanced cm with steps 2 differs from the converged steps-64 rule by 4.09% relative L2. A 62-day full-physics run (2021-12-01 to 2022-01-31) compared steps-2 trapezoids with the Gauss/Fourier default. It used T255 fluxes on 1° LL L117, conservatively regridded to C90, identical convection and PBL inputs, and the CATRINE tracers. Hourly cm differs by 4.21% relative L2 on LL and 1.28% on C90. On C90, caps poleward of 85° contribute 0.12% of the squared difference, and the largest zonal RMS lies near 37°N and 630 hPa. After four weeks the natural-CO2 difference is 0.031 ppm RMS at the surface and 0.0026 ppm in the column, about 0.3% of the accumulated change. The differences are local: zonal-mean differences stay below 0.06 ppm, while the largest single-cell surface differences at week 4 (3.2 ppm natural, 4.5 ppm fossil CO2) lie in one cell near Tehran on the Alborz slope; the SF6 and Rn maxima lie over Central Asian orography. Surface differences level off within the period; column RMS averaged over the final week is 5–11% above that of the preceding week. In monthly means the effect exceeds the restart noise floor at least 80-fold but stays below 3.7% of the difference between the ERA5 and MERRA-2 runs. The error is real and is corrected here, but it does not explain ERA5–MERRA-2 transport differences.

The historical raw trapezoid derivation and day profiles follow.

TM5's default face-integration error is the composite trapezoid error of a coarsely sampled oscillation, not an error in the exact face integral or a CS-only interpolation effect: a 1° V=cos((T−2)λ) probe reproduces −18.7414% / −16.6374%, agreeing with the analytic trapezoid response to roundoff. The code uses 2, despite comments saying 5 points per spectral resolution; even setting 5 leaves −2.5518% / −3.1995%, rather than removing the error.

The inspected source is deps/tm5-mp-r1112/tm5-moguntia-r1112-revised/base/: grid_interpol.F90:1624–1626 defines sT=360°/[2(T+1)], nstep=2 and r=max(1,ceil(nstep·Δ/sT)). Its call-site comments say “5 points per sh resolution” (grid_interpol.F90:1675, also 1820, 2006, 2224, 2713 and 2941). The CarbonTracker tree agrees (base/trunk/src/grid_interpol.F90:1626–1628, comment at 1677). These routines are in grid_interpol, rather than grid_type_sh.F90, which contains the spectral primitives and Nabla bug. IntLat applies the trapezoid to U·Δp/cos⁡φ in latitude (grid_interpol.F90:3248,3275); IntLon applies it to V·Δp in longitude (grid_interpol.F90:3609,3629), with U=ucos⁡φ, V=vcos⁡φ. The common radius/gravity factors do not affect the relative quadrature error.

For 1° faces, TM5-default T255/T639 subdivisions are 3/8, giving spacings 0.333333°/0.125°. The shortest retained longitudinal wavelengths 360°/T are 1.411765°/0.563380°, hence 4.2353/4.5070 samples per wavelength (spacing 0.23611/0.221875 of a wavelength). They are above the Nyquist sampling minimum of two, but far too coarse for accurate trapezoid integration. The following measurements integrate the retained m=T−2 cosine from 0° to 1° with constant pressure thickness. For each sinusoid, the measured relative response equals xcot(x)−1, where x=mΔ/(2r) in radians, to better than 10−12 in relative error.

nstepT255: subdivisions / errorT639: subdivisions / error

A near-sectoral harmonic varying slowly along a meridian can instead expose transverse interpolation error (§10); it does not test this trapezoid defect. The analytic response and direct sums separate those two causes. The reproducible 32-case sweep (nstep=2,3,5,8, four wavenumbers at each truncation) is produced by scripts/diagnostics/tm5_default_quadrature.jl harmonics OUT; its day and native-day commands measure the ERA5 impact below. See scripts/diagnostics/README.md for definitions and commands.

Real ERA5 1° LL day: integration-only comparison. On 2021-12-01, all 24 hourly UTC analyses and all 137 native levels were integrated on every meridian and parallel face, using identical complete wind coefficients and surface pressure on both sides. TM5-default here means the eight-subdivision IntLat/IntLon rule, including its meridian polar endpoint means; the reference uses 16-node Gauss latitude integration and Fourier primitives of longitude products. Doubling to 32 Gauss nodes and 11,520 rather than 5,760 product longitudes at hour 00 (levels 1/70/137) changes U/V relative L2 by only 8.23×10−13 / 3.96×10−16. The independently evaluated review case is −501,352.1089 versus −492,967.1089 kg/s, confirming its 1.7009% difference.

Below, Δ is default minus converged. RMS is unweighted over faces and hours, in kg/s; relative L2 is rms(Δ)/rms(reference). Rates use the IFS radius on both sides, as in the independent review; this common scale does not affect relative errors. Caps are absolute face latitude >85°; meridian faces use interval centres and parallel faces their latitude boundary. The parallel statistics include zero polar rates. The last column excludes absolute latitude ≥89°, separating ordinary trapezoid error from the outer polar interval. The cap meridian discrepancy includes TM5's polar endpoint-mean policy; it must not all be attributed to the sinusoidal trapezoid response above.

about 48 CPU minutes including setup and a discarded partial hour; the two preliminary/convergence passes bring the measurement work to about one CPU hour. Independent hourly chunks reduced wall time; no GPU was used.

Forecast-day filename keys are also distinct from GRIB lead bookkeeping: the older _fc012up2tr3 selector sets start day/hour and lead step at R/tmm_mf_ecmwf_tm5.F90:1655–1677 and C/tmm_mf_ecmwf_tm5.F90:1667–1689. That legacy 00/12 convention is not evidence for NOAA's ERA5 06/18 selection.

14. Validation tolerances ​

BoundaryCriterion
Spectral primitives (analytic)Float64, 10−12 scaled, with an absolute floor tied to the signal scale
QuadratureObserved convergence order matches the rule; the discrete Gauss test (face fluxes against Ck per cell) converges with refinement
Per-layer balance against pydynabout 10−12 scaled; retry decisions exact away from thresholds. FFTW and NumPy FFT differ at rounding level (pydyn/balance.py:9–12), so bitwise equality is not claimed
Closure identity (§7)≤10−12 scaled
Binary and replayexact same-type round trip; replay 10−12 (Float64) and 10−5 (Float32)
Float32 storage conversionwith the synthesis calculation held fixed, equal to that result rounded to Float32

A selected Float32 synthesis/quadrature plan performs its own rounded arithmetic; it need not equal a Float64 calculation rounded only at storage. The CPU selected-precision tests check numerical agreement, replay and the dry pin, not cross-precision bitwise equality. The verified explicit-trapezoid bitwise compatibility covers the previous CPU Float64 payload at matched settings (§13), excluding headers; it establishes neither every precision/backend nor bitwise parity with a Fortran TM5 dump. LL/RG Float32 trapezoids now also use Float32 surfaces and integrands, where the previous implementation used Float64. The shared CPU builder honors explicit Float32 for CS too; unchanged CS quadrature and defaults do not imply unchanged explicitly selected precision.

A tolerance is never loosened to cover a wrong grid, product, basis or missing modes, and an absent or skipped fixture is never reported as passed. pydyn has no spectral stage, so it can check stages 8 and 11 (balance and dynam0) but not stages 3–4. Synthetic pydyn fixtures for stages 8 and 11 are local-only, kept outside the repository and not committed. The parity loader and tests load fixtures from ATMOSTR_TM5_FIXTURES_DIR and skip with a clear message when the variable is unset or the required fixtures are absent.

17. Synthesis backends and measurements ​

Gauss/Fourier executes with a total band budget of 32 target latitude cells, sliced from the existing quadrature geometry. Packed native coefficients are reused across bands; compatible bands refill the same bounded Legendre tables and reuse synthesis/sample buffers. Sequential surface, boundary and forcing Fourier transforms share scratch. Each cell retains its original node order. CPU surface synthesis uses a reusable single-mode panel with the original GEMM dimensions and column positions, preserving its accumulation order without retaining all latitude tables. Native CPU transforms use fixed 32-column GEMMs anchored to global latitude indices, padding partial tiles in both full and streamed execution. Thus band boundaries retain the same GEMM dimensions, leading dimensions and column positions. This avoids the OpenBLAS edge microkernel reductions that otherwise change Float32 and Float64 rounding with band size. CPU streaming retains bitwise equality on the tested CPU/BLAS configurations; this is not a promise of identical bits between different CPU architectures, BLAS versions or FFT libraries. Gauss/Fourier CPU FFTs use aligned scratch for one ring of fields at a time, so their plan shapes also remain independent of band size. This includes the forward and inverse transforms used for Fourier face integrals. These fixed-shape contractions and FFTs can change existing default Gauss/Fourier golden payloads at rounding level; references are not regenerated as part of this correction. Explicit trapezoids retain their existing arithmetic. CPU band pack/scatter/gather uses host loops. Up to four CPU workers divide the cell budget between them, with a fixed two FFT threads each. Plans preserve the global FFTW thread setting; explicit trapezoids keep their existing policy. These CPU measurements do not establish GPU memory fit, bitwise behavior or performance. Bands also limit interior rows to 128, allowing one complete larger cell; the CPU reduces concurrent workers when needed to keep their aggregate interior-row budget at 512 (or one larger cell). Thus coarse cells with more Gauss nodes also stream their tables. The default 32-cell budget is a constant; its division among workers depends on the explicitly configured Julia thread count, never runtime timing or CPU detection. Julia thread count changes scheduling; the two-thread FFT plan setting and native GEMM tiles remain fixed regardless of that division. Golden comparisons must still specify the CPU, precision and library/thread configuration.

After this correction, fresh CPU runs warmed both complete rules before measuring A B A B, with Julia/BLAS/global FFTW threads 16/1/1 and native batch 8:

Both ratios meet the ≤1.5× target. A fresh isolated T639 Gauss/Fourier run peaked at 16.575 GB, 1.120× the retained isolated trapezoid peak of 14.802 GB. Repeated payloads match bitwise, including warmed versus isolated T639 Gauss/Fourier. Explicit Float64 trapezoid payloads at both truncations and the T255 Gauss/Fourier payload retain their prior bits. T639 Gauss/Fourier changes only am, bm, cm, with relative L2 differences of 2.79e-16, 3.06e-16, 1.23e-15 against the prior payload; mass, pressure, humidity and stored time-delta fields remain bitwise equal in this window. The frozen-input default LL72 non-PBL window also changes only am, bm, cm (relative L2 2.15e-16, 2.80e-16, 6.89e-16); other fields and its six-substep schedule are bitwise equal to the retained result. References were not regenerated. These are shared-host, one-window CPU measurements with the §13 inputs; they do not establish full-day or GPU performance.

CPURingSynthesis uses batched host GEMM and unnormalised FFTW; GPUSpectralSynthesis uses the same portable KernelAbstractions pack/scatter/ gather stages, device GEMM and device FFT. Refined samples stay on the device through quadrature. LL/RG synthesis, surface fields, integrands, FFT products and accumulators use the selected precision throughout (Float32 or Float64), including CPU selection. Geometry and reference coefficients are prepared on the host; device kernels introduce no Float64 arithmetic in Float32 plans. After transfer, endpoint pressure is converted to Float64 for the existing host dry pin and closure budgets. Direct CS three-dimensional products and face/overlap gathers accumulate in the selected synthesis precision (Float32 or Float64), including the total accumulator in cs_apply_face_kernel! (src/Preprocessing/Spectral/cs_face_gather.jl:44–58) and the overlap kernel (src/Preprocessing/Spectral/cs_spectral_integrals.jl:33–42). Reduced CS results are then copied to host Float64 endpoint arrays; that copy does not change the accumulation precision. Batches are limited to eight field levels in the day driver. LL/RG Gauss/Fourier packs U/V/D into one transform batch (24 component columns for eight native levels), reusing the Legendre operator and reducing per-mode launches. Explicit trapezoids keep their historical transform sequence. CPU CS surface LNSP, gradients and PS retain Float64; GPU CS surface work follows selected precision. Core does not load CUDA. With CUDA loaded, automatic precision uses Float64 on A100/H100/B200-class devices and Float32 for 3-D fields on L40S-class devices. FAST_MATH is rejected and the CUDA extension selects pedantic math through CUDA.math_mode!, restoring the caller's mode after each transform. GPU execution is opt-in in tests:

bash
ATMOSTR_TEST_SPECTRAL_GPU=1 julia --project=test test/core/test_spectral_synthesis_backends.jl

The preprocessing CLI loads CUDA when this construction requests GPU synthesis. Library callers load their backend explicitly before planning. No silent CPU fallback occurs. The GPU runtime and performance checks require a GPU session; the CPU-array version exercises the portable kernels in ordinary CI. The spike's mirrored-table optimization, pinned staging and copy-free cuFFT execution are performance follow-ups; this implementation uses bounded batches and standard array/FFT APIs.

Device face construction and qualification ​

Backend-dispatched kernels pad native coefficients, construct LNSP gradients and form stable CS polar potentials. Samples, Fourier products and reduced face/cell outputs remain on the selected backend across all native-level batches and latitude bands. The default endpoint API transfers the completed reduced fields to the existing Float64 host pin, vertical merge, Poisson balance and closure. host_output=false exposes the resident arrays for validation. Geometry, cardinal-16 sparse assembly and accurate Legendre table precomputation remain host setup; the legacy nonspectral line-integral API is outside this device path. CPU outputs retain the aligned panels, fixed FFT batches and historical reduction order.

On Float32 device arrays, Neumaier compensation is applied to Gauss latitude sums, Fourier alias folding (real and imaginary parts independently), CS cardinal-16 gathers and conservative overlap sums. Float32 FMA also retains multiplication residuals in these reductions and complex Fourier products. Surface pressure transforms first remove the large constant LNSP mode, then restore its pressure factor when exponentiating the small anomaly. This avoids rounding the full logarithm at every FFT butterfly; scalar host setup prepares the pressure factor. All device correction variables and constants are Float32. Float32 LL/RG device plans also use stable vector harmonics at polar rows. CS GPU surface pressure and gradients now use the selected precision, removing the former compulsory Float64 device surface transform. Pedantic CUDA math wraps the complete operation; FAST_MATH/TF32 remains forbidden. CPU CS surface precision is unchanged.

For a fixed device, library stack and plan shape, deterministic GEMM/FFT algorithms and ordered per-face sums are expected to repeat. Actual bitwise repeatability must be measured on the GPU. Band size changes the device GEMM/FFT batch shapes, so bitwise band independence is not guaranteed; the runner reports both bitwise equality and numerical sensitivity. Neither property is established by CPU emulation.

Float32 compensation cannot recover errors in input conversion, vector coefficients, GEMM, FFT or exp(LNSP). A small retained-mode fixture with a nearly cancelling northward longitude integral has approximately 2.2e-5 relative Float32 error before device compensation. This is an observed residual, not a relaxed scientific bound. The LL/RG Gauss/Fourier CPU Float64 retained-harmonic bound remains 1e-6 per face. CS parity uses the existing cardinal-16 CPU quadrature, with its separately documented arc-discretization error. Actual L40S qualification measures scale-aware raw-face errors and end-to-end balanced fluxes separately.

scripts/validation/gpu_face_quadrature.jl runs the Float32-only L40S qualification. It compares retained rotation, sectoral and off-sectoral edge harmonics and all 137 levels of ERA5 2021-12-01 00 UTC at T255/T639, for LL 1°, reduced Gaussian and C90. CSV files report absolute errors, field-peak-scaled errors, resolved-face relative errors and counts outside 1e-6*abs(reference) + 2e-14*max(field_peak,1); the small absolute term handles symmetry zeros. It also measures repeated results, shape-qualified SHA-256 equality across two fresh Julia GPU processes, and LL/RG band budgets 32 versus 4. Two warmed full production windows per backend cover LL 1° and C90, with 16 Julia CPU threads, BLAS 1, global FFTW 1, production native batches and two FFT threads per CPU band worker. These window times include setup, IO, both endpoints, humidity, balance, closure/replay, positivity and binary writing. CUDA pool high-water marks and whole-device sampled memory peaks have separate labels. See scripts/validation/README.md. For each native level, the face scale is sk=∑f(Ff,kCPU)2/Nf, combining both LL/RG directions and using unique canonical faces on CS. The scale-aware maximum is maxf|Ff,kGPU−Ff,kCPU|/sk; combined horizontal relative L2 is ∥FkGPU−FkCPU∥2/∥FkCPU∥2. This gives a meaningful scale even when one direction vanishes by symmetry. The per-level CSV retains directional relative L2 as an additional diagnostic. The qualification targets are maximum scale-aware face error ≤1e-5 and balanced T639 cm relative L2 ≤1e-4. The latter compares the actual dry, merged, balanced am/bm/cm binary payloads with the CPU Float64 build of the identical 00–01 UTC window, including the same substep schedule. Historical 1e-6 mixed per-face bounds remain diagnostic and do not replace these production criteria. CPU correctness jobs finish before timed windows begin.

L40S qualification (2026-11-03) ​

Actual GPU measurements use an NVIDIA L40S (46068 MiB), driver 615.71.10, Julia 1.12.6, CUDA.jl 5.11.3, CUDA runtime 13.2, CUBLAS 13.4 and CUFFT 12.2. All fields and surfaces use Float32 on the device under pedantic math. The CPU Float64 reference uses the identical quadrature and input coefficients. The real hour is ERA5 2021-12-01 00 UTC, all 137 native levels. Targets are LL 360×180, octahedral RG N64 and C90.

T255 RG ERA5 is slightly above it at 1.105e-5. The strict all-case maximum criterion therefore fails. This is retained in the launcher exit status. Per-level directional and joint L2 values and all historical mixed-bound violation counts remain available in CSV.

Same-plan and two-fresh-process PS/u/v/C arrays match bitwise in every case. LL/RG bands 32 versus 4 change bits; worst face sensitivity is 3.65e-7 of the field peak. CS has no band mode. Captured small LL/CS Float32-kernel PTX (397045 bytes) contains no .f64 registers or instructions. GEMM arrays and FFT plans are Float32; scalar pressure-factor preparation, accurate Legendre tables, geometry, pin, Poisson balance and closure remain host work.

Removing the constant LNSP mode before synthesis reduced T255 LL ERA5 maximum error / level RMS from 2.323e-5 to 1.950e-6 in the pressure-only pilot. PS maximum absolute error fell from 0.2158 to 0.02917 Pa. The final measurements also include FMA product-residual compensation. Both changes are confined to the device Float32 path. Full-day CPU LL72, O24 and C24 goldens retain bitwise equality with origin/main (38af9aca7); eight focused files, quick gate and the structure check pass.

Balanced fluxes, complete-window cost and memory ​

The actual written T639 00–01 UTC dry binaries use 137 native input levels, 34 merged output levels, merge threshold 100 Pa and Float64 storage. CPU/GPU schedules match: 108 substeps on LL and 8 on C90. Each measured GPU binary is compared with the CPU Float64 build of that same window, after humidity, pin, merge, balance, closure/replay, positivity and write.

The strict all-case raw-face maximum still fails. A workflow requiring that universal bound should retain CPU Float64; an optional GPU-synthesis/CPU- Float64-product split needs its own qualification before claiming the bound.

One warmup precedes two measured complete jobs per backend. Both use 16 Julia threads, BLAS 1 and global FFTW 1; CPU Gauss bands retain two FFT threads each. GPU runs use GPU1 plus 16 host threads. CPU correctness jobs finish before timing. Setup, geometry/table preparation, IO and the full production window are included; these are shared-host complete-job costs.

CUDA pool high-water marks are exact over the process lifetime, including warmup; vendor allocations outside that pool are excluded. Whole-device usage is sampled every 100 ms and includes context, reservations and vendor allocations; short transients can be missed. Streamed polar plans and LL host costs ​

Float32 LL/RG workspaces build polar derivative/divided FFT plans once for each compatible band shape. Shapes share one pair of latitude tables sized for the largest polar band; accurate host recurrences refill those tables before the next band executes. Polar sample scratch persists, and native VO/D staging prepares polar coefficients once per endpoint/level batch. This retains bounded latitude-table storage across repeated endpoints. Each shape retains its FFT/sample scratch, while cached polar coefficients scale with the native spectral levels. Other integration temporaries still use backend allocation and GC; the measured pool high-water remains the authoritative memory result.

A GPU1 LL profile after plan reuse captured 8,733 main-thread samples: 42.4% included ring synthesis, 7.4% included CUDA synchronization, and 20.7% included the daily humidity preload. These are overlapping stack fractions from a complete job on the shared host, not isolated phase times. CUDA KA launches, CUBLAS handles and CUFFT plans use the task's current stream. Synthesis now relies on that ordering between pack, GEMM, scatter and FFT, retaining one completion wait per synthesis call; other backends keep their existing barriers.

The matching profile after this change captured 8,768 main-thread samples: 35.1% included ring synthesis, 1.0% CUDA synchronization and 23.0% the humidity preload. Written am/bm/cm payloads were bitwise identical across the scheduling change. Complete profiled jobs took 103.436/104.127 s before/ after with concurrent CPU correctness work, so these profiles establish reduced synchronization overhead, not a complete-job speedup. Final warmed window timings above wait for those correctness jobs to finish.

Remaining performance follow-ups are the host-driven per-order launch/GEMM loop, repeated bounded latitude-table transfers and daily humidity/input IO. The daily preload still reads all 24 hours for a one-window benchmark because that is the production day setup. Chunking inputs or batching spectral orders would need separate implementation and qualification; the 108/8 substep schedules alone do not establish proportional replay cost.

Qualification checks exact case/field/native-level coverage and rejects nonfinite metrics, payloads and timings. Joint horizontal reference RMS must be positive; exact zero references in other fields pass only with zero error and zero scaled metrics. An isolated KA.CPU subprocess enables device staging, polar coefficients, pressure anomalies and Float32 compensation together, including non-unit-product cancellation in a launched gather.

Earlier CPU emulation ​

CPU execution of the complete portable Float32 kernel path on six LL 1° latitude cells (both poles and equator, all longitudes) gives the following maxima across sampled regions. The real hour includes all 137 native levels; these are bounded investigations using BLAS/FFTW, not GPU measurements.

Resolved faces exceed 1e-12*max(field_peak,1) in magnitude. Large relative errors occur in small cancelling fluxes; the per-face bound fails despite small peak-scaled errors. Compensation and stable polar winds are enabled. These earlier CPU-emulation results precede the pressure-anomaly and FMA-product corrections. Actual CUBLAS/CUFFT measurements use the updated qualification runner. The progress file retains absolute errors and counts.

Measured synthetic divergence-identity residuals with explicit trapezoids ||C+H||₂/||C||₂ with refinement steps 2, 4, 8 are 0.0322, 0.00778, 0.00252 on LL and 0.0138, 0.00453, 0.00135 on RG (degree 4, two layers, variable pressure and a truncation-edge divergence mode). Constant-pressure solid-body rotation gives exactly zero C and meridional flux. Degree-7 quirk sizing gives 5.76461 for the sign-only gradient difference with a unit H62 coefficient and 1.77259 for P77(0); a repeated-endpoint cosine mean at 16 longitudes is 0.0588235. These are analytic signal sizes, not climatological errors.

The 2026-10-31 real-wind probe found that point versus face integration changes raw net-divergence RMS by 9–26% in four native layers of one ERA5 window, before balance, pinning and drying. It also measured near-surface polar-cap wind edge differences of about 0.14 m/s in u and 0.176 m/s in v. These establish the importance of face integration and the edge terms; they are not measurements of final balanced cm or tracer differences.
